source_name: Profession.hu company profile - GIRO Zrt. job ads
why_relevant: GIRO Zrt. operates the Hungarian clearing house (GIROInstant/AFR, QVIK). Its hiring for a named workstream signals procurement of external development/ops capacity around national payment infrastructure. A risk-management posting for critical-entity resilience was observed in search results.

source_name: GIRO Zrt. career portal (giro.karrierportal.hu)
why_relevant: First-party hiring feed of the national clearing operator; roles named after systems (GIROInstant, QVIK, IG2) reveal which platform is being built, replaced or externally supplied.

source_name: MKB / MBH Bank career portal (mkb.karrierportal.hu)
why_relevant: A 'Core rendszerszervező' (core system analyst) ad was observed here, describing core-banking development and product implementation - direct evidence of an active core-banking workstream at the MBH group post-merger, which implies vendor engagement.

source_name: karrierportal.hu - shared white-label ATS hosting Hungarian bank career sites
why_relevant: Multiple Hungarian financial institutions run their career sites on <company>.karrierportal.hu subdomains (observed: mkb, giro). Enumerating the subdomain pattern yields a low-noise, first-party hiring feed set for the whole sector.

source_name: MNB Karrier / toborzas.mnb.hu (central bank recruitment portal)
why_relevant: MNB is both regulator and owner of GIRO. Its IT/payment-system role postings foreshadow supervisory-driven programmes (e.g. fraud-detection KVR phases) that cascade into bank-side procurement.

source_name: Indeed Hungary (hu.indeed.com) - employer-scoped searches
why_relevant: Aggregates ads from bank career sites and staffing agencies alike, including agency-posted roles that hide the end client but name the platform ('T24', 'core banking', 'ISO 20022'). Useful for catching vendor subcontracting demand.

source_name: Jooble Hungary (hu.jooble.org)
why_relevant: Secondary aggregator that surfaces ads from smaller Hungarian boards and staffing firms not indexed by Profession; useful redundancy for catching short-lived contractor postings tied to a delivery ramp-up.

source_name: Glassdoor - Budapest banking job listings
why_relevant: English-language postings by international vendors staffing Budapest delivery/nearshore centres - a strong tell that a vendor has won or expects work in the region even before any notice.

source_name: LinkedIn - Magyar Bankholding / MBH Bank company page
why_relevant: Bank and vendor LinkedIn pages publish 'go-live', 'partnership' and team-photo posts that name platforms and integrators months before or instead of a formal notice; employee profiles reveal programme names (e.g. an OTP 'Enterprise Architecture Team Lead - Core Banking Transformation' role was visible in results).

source_name: Dorsum newsroom (Hungarian banking software vendor)
why_relevant: Vendor-side disclosure of contracts that never appear as public notices - Dorsum publicly described its implementation/migration project for Magyar Bankholding (MBH) as the largest in company history. Vendor newsrooms are the most reliable non-notice evidence of an awarded bank IT contract.

source_name: MINDSPIRE Consulting - project office / data migration references (HU)
why_relevant: Hungarian consultancy whose blog and service pages describe its role in domestic instant-payment (AFR) and back-end migration projects - reference pages are effectively an unofficial award log for consultancy contracts at Hungarian banks.

source_name: BÉT / Budapest Stock Exchange disclosure archive (bet.hu KIB filings)
why_relevant: Hosts the authoritative PDFs of listed Hungarian banks' integrated annual reports and quarterly results, where capex / intangible-asset / IT-investment lines and occasionally named technology partners are disclosed - the auditable version of the 'capex fingerprint' signal.

source_name: OTP Bank Investor Relations - annual reports & financial calendar
why_relevant: First-party annual/integrated reports and announcement archive for the largest Hungarian bank; the financial calendar tells you exactly when the next capex-bearing document lands, enabling scheduled collection.

source_name: FinTech Futures - core banking technology desk
why_relevant: Trade press that reports vendor selections for CEE banks, often the only public record of a deal (e.g. reported OTP Bank selecting Intellect/iGCB for a core banking revamp). Ideal cross-check for a hiring or capex signal.

source_name: Finextra press-release wire (vendor announcements)
why_relevant: Vendors self-publish deal and go-live announcements here, including CEE core-replacement programmes (e.g. KBC's Central Europe core replacement timeframe), which cover Hungarian subsidiaries such as K&H.

source_name: Portfolio Financial IT conference - programme & speaker lists
why_relevant: The annual Financial IT agenda is a de-facto actor map: which vendors sponsor, which bank IT executives speak, and which programmes they present. Session titles frequently name in-flight platform projects before any procurement record exists.

source_name: Hungarian Banking Association (Bankszövetség) news & press releases
why_relevant: Sector body announcements about industry-wide programmes (payment scheme changes, joint infrastructure) signal coordinated multi-bank procurement waves; also a canonical member list for actor mapping.

source_name: MNB press releases (payments & banking system)
why_relevant: Regulator announcements of national payment-infrastructure phases (instant payments, central fraud-detection KVR) define the compliance deadlines that force bank-side IT procurement; often the earliest dated anchor for a future contract wave.

source_name: MBH Bank career site (mbhbank.hu / karrier)
why_relevant: MBH is the merged MKB + Budapest Bank + Takarék entity; the post-merger IT consolidation is the single largest Hungarian bank IT programme, and its own hiring is the cleanest indicator of which workstreams are insourced vs. bought.

source_name: MKIK 'Vállalkozz Digitálisan' accredited supplier catalogue (DIMOP Plusz)
why_relevant: Under DIMOP Plusz calls, digital tools and services (including POS/payment-adjacent hardware and software) must be bought from an accredited supplier catalogue maintained by the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce - effectively a pre-qualified vendor register and a demand-side pipeline for SME payment terminal deployments.

source_name: palyazatok.org / cegpalyazat.hu - grant-programme trackers (POS & supplier development)
why_relevant: Grant trackers reveal state-funded demand for POS terminals and supplier-development budgets, which drive terminal-estate procurement volumes at acquirers - a weak but early demand signal.

source_name: IT Business (itbusiness.hu) and its EPA/OSZK archived back-issues
why_relevant: Hungarian IT trade magazine covering vendor-bank deals; complete back-issues are archived as open PDFs at the national library's EPA, giving a searchable historical record of Hungarian bank IT supplier relationships that is unusually easy to mine legally.

source_name: Dun & Bradstreet Hungary company financial reports (api.hungary.dnb.com)
why_relevant: Filed financial data for Hungarian vendor subsidiaries (headcount, revenue jumps) corroborates a delivery ramp-up implied by hiring, and identifies which local entity actually holds a bank contract.

source_name: EBRD Client e-Procurement Portal (ECEPP)
why_relevant: Single mandatory publication point for all EBRD loan/grant-financed procurement, prequalification, shortlisting and contract award notices posted by EBRD clients. Hungarian financial-sector and municipal/energy-efficiency credit-line projects (e.g. lines via Erste Bank Hungary and Raiffeisen Bank Hungary) can generate consultancy and IT/goods notices here that never appear on Hungarian national portals.

source_name: EBRD Procurement Notices (corporate site landing/filters)
why_relevant: Official routing page that explains where notices are published and links onward to ECEPP and to corporate procurement; useful to detect changes in EBRD publication policy that would break a collector.

source_name: EBRD corporate procurement and consultancy services (SMART by GEP)
why_relevant: EBRD's own corporate spend (its consultancy and IT/services purchases, incl. advisory assignments with Hungarian scope) runs through SMART by GEP rather than ECEPP. A separate channel that must be tracked to avoid missing Bank-funded advisory work touching Hungarian banks.

source_name: EBRD Project Summary Documents — Hungary filter
why_relevant: PSDs are published before signing and name the Hungarian client bank, the facility purpose and the technical-cooperation components. They are the earliest reliable leading indicator of procurement that will later surface on ECEPP.
